newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain business leaders more optimistic on economy.
newsitem.headline: Spain business leaders more optimistic on economy.

text.p: Business leaders gave high marks to Spain's economy in a survey published on Wednesday that showed them to be more optimistic about future investment.
"It shows me that an improvement in outlook has taken place in Spain," Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro told journalists at the presentation of the survey in Madrid.
"The outlook has changed and today it's showing itself to be clearly positive."
The survey, the first of its kind by Spain's Association of Business Consultants, looked at a random sample of 405 top executives at 50,000 companies from March to June this year.
It found 97 percent believed the direction of interest rates was very positive for the economy, along with inflation (93 percent) and the public deficit (64 percent).
The study also showed that the business community thought there were bright prospects for the economy in the next six months with 79 percent anticipating an employment rise.
Seventy-seven percent of business leaders said sales had risen in the six months and would continue to go up, with 58 percent of profits up and 62 percent seen rising further.
They were upbeat about levels of present and future private investment, but took a dim view of the drop off in public investment with 45 versus 12 percent seeing it as negative.

Almost all of those surveyed believed Spain would join Europe's economic and monetary union with only one percent thinking it would not enter and 23 percent believing there would be a delay in the start of EMU.

The most credible hypothesis according to the business leaders was that Spain would meet EMU criteria in inflation, interest rates and exchange rates, while there was some doubt that Spain's public deficit and debt levels would qualify.

They gave a positive response to five policies of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar's conservative government: privatisations, control of public spending, structural reforms, labour market reform and employment.
But businesses said that in order to spur further economic development the government should give a higher priority to labour market reform, jobs and public spending controls.
They also found room for improvement in company taxes, investment incentives and infrastructure.

"We can say that the Spanish business leader is optimistic about the macroeconomic situation in Spain and about the future outlook, although there are areas where there could be more action to spur economic development," the survey said in its conclusion.
